Rocky Jones Space Ranger (1954: Entire series available--Groundbreaking early TV Sci-Fi recorded on film--see note in comments)

I am very biased towards this series and find it extremely enjoyable. It basically takes the old sci-fi serials of the 30s & 40s and moves the genre forward. This series was recorded on film (as opposed to video) and it looks MUCH better than most other shows of that era. The stories were told in 3 episode arcs which allowed them to later be edited into ~90 minute "films."

You might think this is a stretch, but I find many parallels between this series and Star Trek. Rocky and his friends were members of the United Worlds of the Solar System (much like the United Federation of Planets). His "crew" was usually comprised of his co-pilot, a kid, a woman, and an old scientist. In many ways it was a family dynamic, much like the dynamic on the Enterprise (and the Love Boat). Rocky was also a two-fisted spaceship captain who was desired by exotic aliens. Again, I know all of that might be a stretch, but it was a unique dynamic at the time that did seem to evolve into a more common sci-fi TV trope.

Finally, make no mistake--this is a kid's show. It is not stupidly juvenile, but it's not high-brow sci-fi. As already mentioned, it is very close in spirit & execution to movie serials.
